blocks.text: Mr. Paolo, the gentleman you have known in book one, is a very smart man. He owns a private school in Venezuela. He married Mrs. Soledad in the spring of 1960 and they have three children: Hector, Gladys and Lorena. The youngest of the three, Lorena, is working in his father’s school and she has a good position there. She is the school’s principal. Gladys is a lawyer, but like Lorena does, she works with her father and goes everyday to school in order to help her parents. She is very intelligent and she takes difficult decisions with absolute authority. Have you asked “What about Hector?” Well, he is terrible in some matters, but he is a good boy too. In fact, all of them are very nice people.

items.q: Is he a very smart man?
Does he have his own school?

items: Betty said: “I am going to study French”. _What did she say?_ She said that she was going to study French.
John said: “I will go to my house”. _What did John say?_ He said that he would go to his house.
Peter said: “I don’t enjoy dancing”. _What did he say?_ He said that he didn’t enjoy dancing.
Ali said: “*I chose this* gift for Helen”. _What did Ali say?_ He said that he *had chosen that* gift for Helen.

blocks.text: What did Alice say? She said that she *loved* to study.
What did Rose say? She said that she had bought a dictionary.
What did the boy say? He said that he *was playing* in the garden.
What did I say? You said that you *had written* some letters.
What did he say? He said that he *would* go to your home.

blocks.title: Exercises: Change to indirect form (reported speech)

items.q: He said “The boys don’t study German”. What did he say?
Mr. Carson said: “They are in this office”. What did he say?
Steve said: “I didn’t take the job”.
She said: “I didn’t take the job”.
Betty said: “It doesn’t fit John well”. What did she say?
Daddy said: “Carol chose the gifts for her mother”. What did he say?
Carl said: “The dogs are sleeping in the garage”. What did he say?

blocks.text: Write these conversations in reported speech

*Mrs. Brown said:* He’s David. He got a cold, a rather bad one, I think. He came back from school yesterday morning. He was hot, so I sent him to bed. He was very ill last night, but he’s a little better this morning.

*Sally said:* He is honest and kind, and he works hard. I was talking to Carter, his manager, the other day. He says Tom is going to do well. He has a good brain, he knows his job and he gets on well with the workers. Carter says he’ll make an excellent manager when he has had a few years of experience.
*Billy:* “I have some money. I’m going to buy an apple and two oranges. I’ll eat them this afternoon. I want to go to Alice’s house because she hasn’t gone to school this week”.
